1.title: Identity Concepts
1.text: Welcome to Module two: Identity Concepts. It covers the exam area Concepts of security, compliance, and identity. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. Define identity as the primary security perimeter. Define authentication. Define authorization. Describe identity providers. Describe the concept of directory services and Active Directory. Describe the concept of federation. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Concepts of security, compliance, and identity (ten to fifteen percent). Exam format: forty-five minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official S C nine hundred study guide, skills measured as of October twenty-one, two thousand twenty-six.

1.title: Identity is the new perimeter
1.text: Identity is the new perimeter. In the past, security relied on a network perimeter: everything inside the office network was trusted. Today users, devices, apps and data are everywhere (cloud, home, mobile), so the network edge no longer protects them. Identity becomes the primary security perimeter: every request is checked by who is asking (the identity), the device and the context.

1.title: Identity is the new perimeter, continued
1.text: Identity is the new perimeter. The figure shows this: From the network perimeter to the identity perimeter.

1.title: Identity is the new perimeter, continued
1.text: Identity is the new perimeter. An identity can be a person (employee, customer, partner), a device, or an application or service. Each needs to prove who or what it is and be given only the access it needs. Exam tip: "Identity is the primary security perimeter" is the Zero Trust idea: verify identity and device for every request instead of trusting the network location.

1.title: Authentication and authorization
1.text: Authentication and authorization. Authentication (Auth N). Question: Who are you? Proving identity. Example: Password plus a code from an app. Authorization (Auth Z). Question: What may you do? Granting permissions after sign-in. Example: Read-only access to a document library. Authentication comes first, then authorization. A person can be authenticated yet not authorized to open a resource. Something you know. Meaning: A secret. Examples: Password, P I N. Something you have. Meaning: A device. Examples: Phone, security key. Something you are. Meaning: A body trait. Examples: Fingerprint, face. Exam tip: Authentication proves identity; authorization grants rights. If a question says "proves who you are" it is authentication; "what you are allowed to do" is authorization.

1.title: Identity providers
1.text: Identity providers. An identity provider (I D P) creates, maintains and manages identities and authenticates users for applications. When an app trusts an I D P, users sign in at the I D P and the app receives proof (a token). Microsoft Entra I D. The Microsoft cloud identity provider. Active Directory. The traditional on-premises directory. Social providers. For example sign-in with a personal account. An I D P gives single sign-on: sign in once and reach many apps.

1.title: Directory services and Active Directory
1.text: Directory services and Active Directory. A directory service is a central database of identities and resources (users, groups, devices) with rules for access. Where. Active Directory Domain Services (A D D S): On-premises: domain controllers. Microsoft Entra I D: Cloud. Protocols. Active Directory Domain Services (A D D S): Kerberos, N T L M, L D A P (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol). Microsoft Entra I D: oh auth, sam el, Open I D Connect and H T T P S. Main use. Active Directory Domain Services (A D D S): Sign-in to Windows domain resources. Microsoft Entra I D: Sign-in to cloud and web apps. Structure. Active Directory Domain Services (A D D S): Domains, trees, forests, O U s, Group Policy. Microsoft Entra I D: A tenant with users, groups and apps (flat, no O U s or Group Policy).

1.title: Directory services and Active Directory, continued
1.text: Directory services and Active Directory. Active Directory is Microsoft's on-premises directory service. Microsoft Entra I D is not a cloud copy of A D D S: it is a cloud identity and access management service built for web protocols. Exam tip: A D D S equals on-premises, Kerberos and L D A P. Entra I D equals cloud, oh auth and sam el. Many organizations use both (hybrid identity, module three).

1.title: Federation
1.text: Federation. Federation is a trust relationship between two organizations or systems so that a user who is authenticated by one can access resources of the other without a separate account. Identity provider. Authenticates the user and issues a token. Service provider (relying party). The app that trusts the token. Federation makes S S O across organizations possible: a partner's employee signs in with their own company credentials and gets access to your app. Standards include sam el, oh auth two point zero and Open I D Connect.

1.title: Federation, continued
1.text: Federation. The figure shows this: Federation: a user signs in at their identity provider and the app trusts the token. Exam tip: Federation equals trust between identity systems so a user needs one set of credentials. The I D P authenticates; the app trusts the I D P.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors staff work from home and use cloud apps. Why is the network perimeter no longer enough? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Users, devices and data are outside the office network, so identity must be verified. When resources are everywhere, identity becomes the primary perimeter.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A user signs in with a password and a code and then opens a file. The system checks that the user has read access. Which step is the check? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Authorization. Deciding what an authenticated user may do is authorization.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which component creates and manages identities and authenticates users for applications? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: An identity provider. An identity provider manages identities and authenticates users.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which statement about Active Directory Domain Services is true? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: It is an on-premises directory that uses Kerberos and L D A P. A D D S is the traditional on-premises directory service.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A partner's employees sign in to Fabrikam's app with their own company accounts. Which concept makes this possible? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Federation. Federation is a trust between identity systems so users can use one identity across organizations.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A user has a phone that receives a code. Which authentication factor is the phone? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Something you have. A device the user possesses is a possession factor.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Why is identity called the primary security perimeter? Answer: Because users, devices and data are outside the office network, so access is decided by identity. Question two. What is the difference between authentication and authorization? Answer: Authentication proves who you are; authorization decides what you may do. Question three. What does an identity provider do? Answer: Creates and manages identities and authenticates users.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Name the on-premises and the cloud Microsoft identity services. Answer: Active Directory Domain Services and Microsoft Entra I D. Question five. What is federation? Answer: A trust between identity systems so one sign-in works across organizations. Question six. Name the three authentication factor types. Answer: Something you know, have and are.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Identity perimeter: identity (person, device, app) replaces the network edge as the main boundary. Auth N versus Auth Z: who you are versus what you may do; factors: know, have, are. Identity provider: creates and authenticates identities; gives S S O. Directory services: A D D S on-premises (Kerberos, L D A P); Entra I D cloud (oh auth, sam el, Open I D Connect). Federation: trust between identity systems; I D P authenticates, app trusts the token. In the next module, we continue the course.
